pr_title: Skip unsupported LIFX Switches during discovery
pr_body:
This resolves an issue with the underlying library waiting for
a response from the switches that will never arrive.

Signed-off-by: Avi Miller <me@dje.li>

## Proposed change

This change adjusts the discovery of LIFX devices so that switches are skipped. This is due to the underlying `aiolifx` library's lack of support for switches and the core integration's assumption that all LIFX devices are bulbs. The `bulb.get_color` call will hang for about 2-3 minutes for each switch discovered without this fix.

### The problem

I have an issue with LIFX integration getting error like this:

```
Logger: homeassistant.components.lifx.light
Source: components/lifx/light.py:382 
Integration: LIFX (documentation, issues) 
First occurred: 5 ottobre 2021, 20:45:52 (3678 occurrences)
Last logged: 5 ottobre 2021, 23:12:28

Failed to initialize 192.168.1.115
```

the strange thing is that restarting the bulb (few times) it gets back online in HA, once online it is stable as long as I try to restart HA core which upon restart fails to initialize the bulb.
The bulb is online as I can ping and control via LIFX IOS App.


### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2019.9.7

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2019.8.x (I think)

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

LIFX

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/lifx/

```yaml
N/A
```

I've just pushed a significant update to the LIFX Beta integration released as v2.1 over at https://github.com/Djelibeybi/ha-lifx-beta. In particular, you can now configure your own discovery interval and retry/timeout values. 

The defaults are only acceptable for ~5 bulbs: anything more than that, and you'll be in almost a continuous packet storm as each discovery process just stacks on the packets from the last one. I've added some notes on how to calculate the discovery interval, but for my network of 60 bulbs, the minimum acceptable interval is around 180 seconds (3 minutes).

It also adds a bunch of debug logging for nerds, if you like that sort of thing.

Finally, it avoids a networking issue that I suspect is affecting anyone who has a Raspberry Pi or similar device with both the ethernet and wifi adapters enabled and connected to the same network. The existing integration will send broadcasts on both interfaces, but bulbs will only reply to one. This leads to packet loss, retries and confusion. The Beta integration will only use one interface per broadcast network to avoid this issue.

The challenge is that the trigger for discovery is a single broadcast packet and then the flood gates open in response.

I'm not sure I've explained the actual problem properly. The issue isn't the initial discovery itself, it's what that discovery triggers and how well the bulbs respond to it that makes a difference. Even on a completely hardcoded instance with zero discovery, the problem is still possible, though admittedly greatly reduced.

Once the bulbs have been found, it takes anywhere between 4 to 24 additional messages for the bulbs' capabilities to be fully established. The existing core integration does some caching and assuming a bulb never goes offline, should only ask for that level of detail once a minute or so.

The beta will soon use a sliding scale for different pieces of information. It will check Color/Power most often, say every 10 seconds, followed by various other states like whether the bulb is running an effect or transitioning to another state, or has had its name or group membership changed, etc. These last items may only be checked every 5-10 minutes.

I've been working with and recently contributing to another LIFX library called [Photons](https://github.com/delfick/photons), which is significantly more advanced than the library currently being used by the integration. In the background, I'm also tinkering with a complete replacement integration powered by Photons that has the potential to include features like locally controlled scenes, effects and animations for Tile, Candle and Beam devices.

TL;DR: the problems are annoying but known and can be mitigated. It's just going to take a bit of time for me to learn more about Home Assistant and how best to do that in this context.
